thesis.html.one_line: The flagship research piece, but in its current form it is an abstract stretched to page length. It has no methods, no literature, no figure and no uncertainty, and nearly every number appears three or four times. It should be rebuilt as a proper thesis summary rather than trimmed.
must_fix: No uncertainty anywhere. The AR(2) sums 0.727/0.715, the 33-min half-life, the 5.6 %/2.3 % RTI shares and the 204/60/182/40 CZK figures have no SE, CI or cluster count. At minimum, report route-clustered CIs for the persistence sums and the RTI shares.

Estimation is not described. The page never says what t indexes (consecutive stops of one trip? 5-min bins?), whether the AR(2) is pooled or route-level, which fixed effects and time-of-day seasonal terms are included, or how panel dynamic bias (Nickell) is handled given JEL C23. The equation in 'Serial correlation in Prague's delays' has no intercept, route effects or seasonal term, yet the next section decomposes variance into 'a seasonal part, a forecastable state and unforecastable noise'. Add a short 'How this was done' section, as long-articles.md requires.

'Registered' is overclaimed. The facts say '3 of 3 registered in the proposal', and 'The three hypotheses from the proposal' calls them 'registered'. A thesis proposal is not a pre-registration. Either link the dated proposal (IES SIS record) or say 'stated in the thesis proposal'. Cut the non-sequitur 'That all three failed in their registered form ... shows that the questions could not have been re-chosen once the answers were known'. Failing hypotheses do not prove the questions were fixed in advance; a timestamp does.

H3 contradicts itself: 'the null is real, but a failed placebo leaves the result conditional on education being entangled with network structure.' A null with a failed placebo is not 'real'. Call it inconclusive, or use the registered wording.
H1: 'the gap between bus and tram is a quarter of the smallest effect the design could reliably detect'. State the MDE and the observed gap in numbers.
No link to the thesis PDF (IES/CUNI repository) and no code path. A stranger cannot reproduce anything. Add the repository DOI or handle, a code repo link and a Golemio access date and endpoint.

Zero external literature, and both references are self-citations. The opening claim that 'the value-of-reliability literature prices travel-time variability with its unconditional standard deviation' needs primary sources (e.g. Noland & Small 1995; Bates et al. 2001; Fosgerau & Karlström 2010; Carrion & Levinson 2012 review). The value-of-RTI claim needs its own comparators (e.g. Brakewood & Watkins 2019).

Unit inconsistency across the site: this page says '121 197 794 vehicle-location records', while delayed.html calls the same data '121 M stop events'. These are different objects. Pick the correct one and use it on both pages.
The deck says 'This is the short version', which contradicts the house-style rule that each article exists in one form. The deck should state the question and the finding.
cut: The tldr box. Its five bullets are near-verbatim copies of the four body sections; 'These figures index the dispersion made forecastable, not a welfare gain a passenger has been measured to pocket' appears twice word for word. Cut it, or reduce it to one line if the page is restructured.

The section 'Why the record on this site plays the delays'. It is a site-housekeeping aside and a closing moral ('the right product is a live view'), and 'They are not predictable in the way a prediction pipeline hopes' sits awkwardly next to the thesis's own point that a fraction of the dispersion is forecastable.
The sentence 'The contribution is a method that transfers beyond Prague...' in 'Limits of the estimates'. It belongs in the opening section as the contribution statement, not among the limitations.
The repetition of 0.727/0.715. It appears in the meta, the facts, the tldr, the body and the equation. Keep the facts line and the equation.
missing: An explicit research question and contribution paragraph, placed relative to the literature (what is new: a conditional-variance correction rather than a multiplier; RTI valued without stated preference).

At least one figure: the impulse response with a band, or a stacked bar of the variance decomposition by mode (seasonal / state / noise). It should carry a caption and a data-view hook like the other articles.
A hypothesis table (H1–H3: prediction, result, registered wording), which the house style lists as a genuine table.
Robustness: the out-of-sample date split is mentioned only in passing (182/40 CZK). Say what the split was and how RTI shares behave out of sample.
Calibration constants used for the CZK levels (value of time, reliability ratio, trips per year, the commuter tier) with sources.
The metro result itself, which is only mentioned as excluded. Report it descriptively with its caveat.
Data section: Golemio API/feed, access date, cleaning (dedup, clipping), and how many routes and trips were dropped.

delayed.html.one_line: A charming, well-documented sonification with good code availability. It is a creative side project, not research, and it currently borrows the thesis's authority with a statistical sentence that is wrong. Trim it and move it to a notes or projects category.
must_fix: The statistics are wrong. 'A shock to the delay at one moment is still three-quarters there in the next' misreads the AR(2): the one-step response is φ1, not φ1+φ2, and the thesis's time step is never given. The same paragraph says 'Statistically the state is an autoregression whose coefficients sum to 0.73', which conflates the thesis's route-level trip dynamics with the city-wide 5-min averages the record plays. Either state the link loosely and correctly, or drop the equation.
'the ear picks it up before the table does' is an unsupported claim. Cut it.

The facts headline '121 M stop events' inflates the source. The record plays five days, about 3.27 M events by the track table. Lead with the five days, and fix the unit conflict with thesis.html ('vehicle-location records').
The chorus rule is circular: 'On a typical weekday that rule yields exactly the two rush hours'. Say whether the 68 % threshold was chosen to produce that result; if it was, say it was tuned.

The day-selection criteria are missing. How were the five days picked? What makes 17 Jun 'the most median day'? What happened on 30 Apr ('The Meltdown', 164 s)? Give one factual sentence on its cause, or say it is unknown.
The thesis link goes to '../#works' instead of 'thesis'. Link the article.
The key naming is inconsistent. The rule lists 'ionian' but the track table says 'D major' for the Summer Sunday. Use one name.
The trains row says 'Still shown in the chart', but fig. 1 plots surface transport only. Say which chart is meant (the player's), or delete the phrase.

The mean arrival delay includes negative (early) values and is clipped to [−600, 3600] s. That belongs in the text, not only in ref 2, because early running offsets lateness in the 'mean delay' that sets each key.
cut: The tldr box. It repeats the deck, the facts, both tables and the figure caption.
The zinger 'Any resemblance to an actual banger is purely statistical', and 'played as disco tracks by the transport system itself', which personifies the data. Both break the house style.
The triple statement that no raw records are redistributed (tldr, first section, ref 2). Say it once.
The footer 'Figure.' paragraph, which duplicates the fig. 1 caption and ref 2. Merge them into the caption.
The production-notes paragraph (58 % shuffle, side-chain, −4.5 dB shelf at 6 kHz). Keep one sentence and link the README.
missing: Golemio access date and licence name (the page says 'please credit Golemio' but gives no licence).
A one-line statement of what each non-bus instrument maps (the tram and trolleybus rows say only 'stop events': count? delay? both?).
An audio embed or clip on the page itself, so the reader hears it without leaving.

quotecheck.html.one_line: The strongest of the four. It has a real incident, a precise mechanism, real CLI runs and a tool whose 20 tests match the text. It needs its overclaims and zingers cut, the drift metric specified, the Frankl sourcing fixed and the short-version box removed.
must_fix: Deck: the three sentences about failures ('One day a quotation reached it...', 'The checker written the next day then nearly deleted...', 'Both failures are in the tool now...') are a run of short declaratives for effect. Rewrite them as two sentences of prose that name the tool, what it checks and the one headline result (Frankl ABSENT, 292 passages re-checked).

Short-version box ('Overwhelmed? Here's the short version'): its five bullets repeat the deck, the facts panel and the 'What it does not do' paragraph almost word for word, including the 80 % threshold and 'only as good as the extraction'. Drop the box on a ~1,500-word tool piece. At the least, retitle it: 'Overwhelmed?' is chatty, not house style.

Section 'A fabricated ISACA quotation': 'A fabrication tailored to a brief always looks like the best result in the report' overclaims with 'always' from a single case. Restate it as an observation about this case.

Section 'Splices': the closing line 'The six classes of false alarm turned out to be one bug: the tool had been comparing transcriptions rather than words.' is a colon-reveal zinger. It also sits in the wrong section, since it concerns the false-alarm section and not splices. Cut it, or fold it into 'Six classes of false alarm' as a plain sentence.

Section 'Folding, the four answers...': DRIFT is defined as 'at least 80 % similar' without naming the measure. The code uses difflib.SequenceMatcher.ratio() on folded windows (find.py, DRIFT_FLOOR = 0.80). Say so, because the threshold is meaningless without the metric.

Reference 4 (Frankl): it asserts the sentence 'does not appear in any edition', but the evidence offered is one edition (Beacon Press). Narrow the claim to what was checked, and cite a primary or documented secondary source for the misattribution history (e.g. Quote Investigator's entry, with access date) rather than 'widely reported' and 'usually traced'.
'1910 is content in Stoner' refers to a book that appears nowhere in the references or the runs. Either add it as a source or pick an example from the four books cited.

Reference 1 is the author's account of a private log. State plainly in the text that the 292-passage re-check and the 'sixteen defects, fourteen splices' count cannot be verified externally, and give the date of the count.

Reproducibility: the four runs need copyrighted full texts (the CISA manual, East of Eden, etc.) that a reader cannot obtain from the repo. Say this, and point to the test fixtures in the repo as the reproducible substitute.
cut: The short-version box (see must_fix).
Facts row 'tests: 20 one per class, plus the cases that must fail'. It duplicates the stack line 'pytest (20)'. Keep one of the two.
'which is the test a lenient checker has to pass before its FOUND can be trusted' (end of the runs paragraph). It is a closing moral.
'Nothing normalised is ever shown, and that is what keeps a forgiving search honest'. Keep the fact, cut the 'keeps ... honest' flourish.
The literal 'cross-\nvalidation' renders as a backslash-n. Either show it as a real line break or describe it in words.
missing: A sentence on prior art: fuzzy matching and quotation-verification tools (difflib / rapidfuzz, citation-checking work in LLM hallucination evaluation) and why a folding-plus-offset-map approach differs.
Any measured error rate, e.g. over the 292 re-checked passages: how many FOUND, FOUND*, DRIFT and ABSENT, and how many were confirmed by hand. Right now the tool's accuracy rests on anecdotes.
The package version number and access dates for the PyPI and GitHub links.
A link to the second-brain article, which tells the same ISACA incident under a different tool name (quote.py).

sitewitness.html.one_line: A solid engineering log with honest run-by-run misses. It is framed as an evaluation it cannot support: the final score only matches the old Worker's 29/30, the golden set changed between runs, and the intermediate scores exist only in terminal output. The prose also carries several slogans.
must_fix: The facts panel says '6 evaluation runs' but lists five scores ('22 → 26 → 26 → 28 → 29 of 30'), and the text covers runs 1–5 only, with the fourth run 'of the day' cut off by budget. Reconcile the count: say what run 6 was, or which run was truncated and what it scored.

Evaluation validity. The golden-set expectations were changed during the series (run 1: jobs five→six and '3,704 vs 3704'; run 5: '2 263 vs 2262.5' called 'the evaluator's fault'). The scores 22→29 are therefore not measured against a fixed instrument. Either re-score every run against the final golden set, or state that the numbers are not comparable. Also report that the endpoint (29/30) equals the old Worker's 29/30 (eval-history.json, 2026-09-17), so the package matched rather than improved accuracy. Say that explicitly instead of implying progress.

n = 30 with one question per 'quote' kind (eval-history by_kind: quote n=1). A one-question difference is noise. Give the uncertainty (e.g. 29/30, 95 % CI roughly 83–99 %), and stop reading single-question flips as findings.

Reproducibility: the reference admits the intermediate scores 'are from the terminal output'. Only the 17 Sept (Worker) and 22 Sept runs are in ask/eval-history.json. Publish the per-run eval JSONs, or mark the 22/26/26/28 figures as unrecorded.
eval-history.json shows protocol_violations: 1 on the 22 Sept run, the final run the page implicitly reports. Mention it, and say which rule fired.

Closing paragraph: 'Nor does it make the model right; it makes the model's wrongness visible and refusable, which on the evidence of the detector text is the most a run-time system can do.' This is a banned 'not X but Y' construction plus an unsupported general claim resting on another article. Cut it, or state the specific result from silent-detector with a number.

H1 'An agent that shows its work.' ends with a period and is a slogan. The <title> reads 'sitewitness: an agent that shows its work'. Make them one descriptive title, e.g. 'sitewitness: rules enforced in code for a site Q&A agent'.
Numbered headings ('1 · Five rules...', '2 · What the golden set found...') are inconsistent with the other articles in the family. Drop the numerals.
Name the model (eval-history: claude-sonnet-5) and the date in the text. Scores and costs are model-specific.
cut: The short-version box. It restates the deck, the facts panel and the closing paragraph (the no-streaming limitation and the 'visible and refusable' line appear twice).

Facts row 'security findings: 5 from review, all fixed before the first deploy'. It repeats section 3's first sentence. Also consider folding section 3 into one paragraph under 'Running it': the security fixes are routine hardening, not a contribution.
'what any agent needs and most demos skip' (section 1): slogan.
'all real and all cheap' (section 3): rhythm pair.
'which showed that a rewrite that looks equivalent is not necessarily equivalent, and that only a fixed test can tell' (section 2): moral, and ironic given that the test was not fixed.
'which also showed that the budget works' (end of section 2): a trivial finding presented as one.
missing: Contribution relative to existing practice: rule-based output guards and grounding checks (e.g. Guardrails AI, NeMo Guardrails, citation-grounding evals such as RAGAS faithfulness), and what enforcing in code adds.
The false-refusal rate: how often a rule replaced a correct answer, per rule, in the final run. It is the cost side of 'enforced in code' and the most informative number the design could give.

A limitations paragraph proper. The golden set was written by the author for her own site, so the questions are in-distribution. The rules are lexical (a 'digit in the answer' heuristic, a 40-character quote threshold) and can be passed by paraphrase.
The package version and access dates; links to the golden.json and eval.py files already in the repo (ask/golden.json).

filmrunner.html.one_line: A product write-up with no question, no measurement and only private references. Its facts are stale against the repo (nine ADR files, not five) and it contradicts itself on 'open source'. It is honest material for a notes or portfolio entry, not a journal-grade article.
must_fix: The kicker says 'live demo · open source', but references 1 and 3 say 'private repository'. One of these is false. Fix the kicker or publish the repo.

'five architecture decision records' (facts panel, short version and body) is out of date. docs/adr/ in the repo now holds nine files (ADR-001 twice, as backend-stack and frontend-stack, plus ADR-006 to ADR-008 on location services, web push and public rate limiting). Update the count and the list.

'An independent security review found two problems': say who or what reviewed, when, and in what scope. 'Independent' is unsupported, and the reference is 'as recorded in the project; repository private'.

'it is the one document all 50 to 200 people need before they leave home' and 'conventions that are decades old and load-bearing' have no source. Cite an industry reference (e.g. a DGA or production-handbook source on call sheets and eighths), or drop the figures.

The deck opens in the first person with a slogan ('I built a whole film-production platform... Then I cut it down to the one document that actually decides whether a shoot day works'). Rewrite it as two plain sentences of prose.
'so the sheet has to be a container of ordered revisions, not one mutable row' is a 'not X but Y' device. State the design choice directly.
cut: The short-version box. Four of its five bullets are paragraphs of the body lightly reworded (first build, security review, second build, what it leaves out).
The paragraph 'The company itself runs as one founder and an AI team...'. It is off topic for a call-sheet article and unsupported. It belongs, if anywhere, on an about or process page.
The facts row 'studio-readiness track: SSO · DPA · Sentry', which re-lists the first-build paragraph.
The live-demo section can be two sentences appended to 'The second build'.
missing: Any evidence the wedge works: a user test with an AD or crew, a timed offline load, the number of revisions handled on a real or simulated shoot day. Without that it is a feature list.
Why the first build was cut: the decision and its rationale (ADR or DESIGN.md scope note), stated in the text rather than only referenced.
Prior art: StudioBinder, Movie Magic, Set Hero and similar call-sheet tools, and what this one does differently (offline PWA, revision container).
Access dates, and public links for anything cited, or a clear statement that the reader must take it on trust.

second-brain.html.one_line: An interesting practice, but written as a showcase. Its two 'findings' are unverifiable and one rests on a reproducibility/reproduction equivocation. It re-tells the quotecheck incident under a different tool name and ends on hype. Either tighten it into a method note that points to quotecheck, or merge the incident material into quotecheck and keep this as a short notes entry.
must_fix: Finding 2, the EU GPAI Code of Practice 'asks for reproducibility in one appendix and forbids reproducing training data in another', conflates reproducibility of results or documentation with regurgitation of training data. A referee would read it as a pun, not a tension. Either quote both passages with section numbers and explain why they actually conflict, or drop it.

Finding 1, 'the setting most likely to leak fine-tuned data is a decoding parameter', needs a primary citation (e.g. Carlini et al. 2021, 'Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models'; Nasr et al. 2023) and a section-level citation of NIST AI 600-1 showing the omission. Reference 4 currently says only 'findings as recorded on the wiki's pages', which a reader cannot check.

Inconsistency with quotecheck.html: this page says the fix was 'quote.py' and that the fabrication 'survived several passes'. The quotecheck page says the fix was the quotecheck package and that the quotation 'survived the checks that existed', with 292 passages re-checked. Use one name and one account, and link the quotecheck article instead of re-telling the incident.

Deck: 'Retrieval re-derives knowledge from raw documents on every question, and nothing accumulates' is an unsupported strawman of RAG. 'Obsidian serves as the IDE, the LLM as the programmer and the wiki as the codebase' is a borrowed triad slogan. Attribute it to Karpathy or cut it.

'which produced a code review as good as any I have had' is hype. 'The verdict, written by a page that had been compiled that morning from a database textbook' personifies a page. State what the review found, in one sentence, with a pointer.
Verify the date of the Karpathy gist given as 2026, and add access dates to both GitHub references.
cut: The short-version box. It repeats the deck and the facts panel, and its third bullet copies the 'Two findings' paragraph almost verbatim, including 'Neither is a contradiction inside one document'.
The facts row 'caught: 1 fabricated quote and a tool so it cannot happen again'. 'Cannot happen again' overclaims; quotecheck itself says splices and bad extractions still get through.
The paragraph on thirteen subagents, unless it can carry a concrete, checkable result.
The whole 'A fabricated quotation' section, reduced to one sentence linking quotecheck.html.
missing: A stated question or claim the page supports, e.g. whether ingest-once integration catches cross-document tensions that per-question retrieval misses. At least one worked example with the actual linked pages quoted would show it.

Quality measures for the wiki itself: the lint results over time (orphans, broken links, drift counts), the share of pages with verified quotations, and error rates found in audits. The counts (739 pages, 8 144 links, 336 sources) measure size, not quality.
Limitations: a private vault (nothing is checkable), a single author and single agent, possible confirmation bias in what the wiki 'surfaces', and the cost and time per ingest.
Relation to prior work beyond Karpathy's gist: personal knowledge management literature, and LLM-maintained knowledge bases and memory systems.

surf.html.one_line: A sound verification protocol presented as findings: the page reports no results, its headline base rate (5 of 92, 5 %) is already out of date against surf/data.json (14.2 % of 106 days), and it describes the robustness grid as computed when data.json has robustness: {}. Rewrite it as a dated protocol plus tool note, or hold it until lead 1 to 6 skill exists.
must_fix: Stale numbers throughout. The facts row, the short-version box and the sections 'The surfable rule and the summer at Ericeira' and 'The booking decision as expected value' say 'five surfable days in 92 ... 5 %'. surf/data.json (generated 2026-09-28) gives 106 days and surfable_share 0.142. The sensitivity shares in the article (2 % / 19 % / 4 % / 5 % / 11 %) differ from data.json (8.5 % / 25.5 % / 12.3 % / 14.2 % / 18.9 %). Either freeze the article to a named snapshot ('as of 13 September 2026, 92 days') everywhere, or read the numbers from data.json. As it stands the prose contradicts the live page it links to.

Overclaim in 'Sensitivity to the surfable rule': 'The binary results are recomputed under five alternative rules' and 'The skill numbers will be shown under every one of these rules'. data.json has robustness: {}. State this as planned and not yet implemented.

'There are no skill numbers yet' is also out of date: lead 0 now has n = 14 for every spot and model (e.g. Ericeira MFWAM MAE 0.114 m, Spearman 0.93; BSS vs climatology 0.925). Lead 0 is close to self-verification and is not the booking-relevant lead. Say that explicitly, rather than implying nothing exists.

The persistence baseline is ill-defined at lead 0. 'Persistence taking the forecast for lead d to be the analysis d days before the target' makes persistence equal to the truth at d = 0, yet data.json reports bss_vs_persistence 0.722 at lead 0. Define persistence at d = 0 or exclude lead 0 from it.

Block bootstrap by ISO week (500 resamples) at 14 pairs covers two to three blocks, so the intervals are meaningless. data.json indeed has mae_swell_ci95: None. State the minimum number of weeks before an interval is shown, not just the 14-pair gate.

Pre-registration status. 'Expectations recorded on 14 September 2026' needs a verifiable timestamp: a commit hash or file path in the repo. Also state the pass/fail criterion for each claim, e.g. 'most days' in claim 1 is not operational.

The decision model treats n days as independent draws at the same p. A two-day trip needs the joint or expected count of surfable days, and p is per-day. Add this assumption, or define p as the expected share of surfable trip days.
The data sources (Open-Meteo, EMODnet) have no access dates. r4 has one (14 Sept) but r2 does not.
cut: Short-version box: it repeats the deck, the facts row and every section's first sentence. Cut it, or reduce it to one line pointing to the live page.

The 'Data engineering' section (5 paragraphs): idempotency, 8 KB a day, 'costs nothing' and pytest details belong in the repo README. Keep two sentences (append-only, aggregation at ingest, 6 synthetic tests) and link to them.

The duplicated proxy-truth caveat. It appears in the short version, 'What is stored each morning', 'Sensitivity...' paragraph 2, and again in the data-engineering 'If a buoy feed appears' line (said twice). State it once, in a limitations section.
The footer 'Figure.' note repeats the last paragraph of 'Data engineering' ('so the figure and the page cannot disagree' appears twice).

Slogans and closing morals: kicker 'a page that gets better every morning'; 'six days out it is guessing with confidence'; 'the forecast at flight-booking lead is a coin with a bias' (inside a registered claim, which should be neutral); 'That base rate is the honest prior, and the page exists because...'; 'which would be worth knowing'; 'and the page will show it arriving'.
The decision-inputs table largely duplicates the paragraph above it. Keep one of the two.
missing: Literature. Wave-model verification against buoys (e.g. Bidlot et al. on ECMWF WAM verification; Janssen), and multi-model ensembles with 3 members as probability forecasts, including their calibration limits. The contribution relative to existing surf-forecast verification (e.g. Surfline/Magicseaweed accuracy studies) is not stated.

A limitations section in house structure ('What this does not show'): proxy truth; one summer season versus the autumn ground-swell regime; a 3-member 'probability' limited to 4 values; daylight aggregation; a 3-spot sample.
A timeline: the date when each lead reaches 14 and 30 pairs (lead 6 reaches 14 on about 4 October), and when the three claims will be read.
The exact code path for the tests (surf/tests/test_verify.py) and the command to reproduce data.json.
A statement that the 92-day climatology is back-filled analysis, not stored forecasts. The collector started 14 Sept but the analysis starts 14 June.

brand-reflection.html.one_line: A portfolio hub that summarises four weekend studies hosted elsewhere, with no uncertainty, no limitations section, several overclaims, and a slogan title. Cut it to a short, sober index of the studies plus the prediction check, and move it to notes.
must_fix: Title and deck are slogans: 'Strategy decks talk about brand. This measures it.' Replace with a content title, e.g. 'Colour, sound and homepage language in 47 Czech TV spots'.
Episode 1 overclaim: 'The twenty in between are the main finding, since they show that most Czech spots do not choose'. 20 of 47 is 43 %, not most.

Threshold inconsistency. Paragraph 1 says 'Beyond about 90° the two are, perceptually, different colours' and fig. 1 draws a 90° line, but the classification uses <20° and >100° (tools/brand_figures.py). Justify the 20/100 cut-offs, or report the counts at 90°. The 20-degree band has no stated rationale.

'brands cluster across sector boundaries by their colour signature' and 'Saturation tension ... does split by category' are given no statistic: no cluster validity measure, no test, no number. Add numbers or drop the claims.

Episode 2: the distinguishing words for the 'institutional register' cluster are 'banka, škoda, čez, fio, česká'. These are brand and sector names, which suggests the embedding is clustering on names, not register. This undermines 'one institutional register'. Also, 'A challenger bank's positioning ... is decided in the campaign layer and quietly undone in the homepage layer' is an interpretive leap from 24 scraped pages.

'27 of 47 minor' is presented as a skew. It is 57 % (binomial p ≈ 0.4 against 50 %). Krumhansl–Schmuckler on voice-dominated audio (44 of 47 spots are voice-led) is also unreliable. Drop the claim or report it with a caveat.

Prediction check. The registered claim was over thirty days (check due 17 June), but it was run at 119 days, so this is not the registered test. With the Lidl spot private, claim A is indeterminate, not 'holds on paper' (3 813 vs 3 210 compares 2 coherent spots with 2 muddled ones). Use registered wording: 'claim A: indeterminate (one of three coherent spots unmeasurable, window deviated from 30 to 119 days); claim B: not supported'.

Promotional language to remove: 'a tool a strategist can use on Monday'; 'would have little competition in the category' (a strategy recommendation not supported by the data); 'What I would keep from the exercise is the habit...' (closing moral).
No access dates for YouTube data, no date for the homepage scrape, and no source for the brand anchor swatches.
cut: Short-version box: all five bullets repeat the facts row and the body. Cut it.
The Spot Scorer section. The tool description can be one sentence with a link. Fold the Pilsner/Albert paragraph into Episode 1.5 or the fig. 3 caption.
Episode numbering '1 / 1.5 / 2' plus 'four artifacts' in the kicker: this is internal project jargon.
The fig. 2 caption 'Three cross the line' repeats the body text.
The intro sentence 'The series was built across a few weekends...' is fine for notes, but it confirms this is not journal research.
missing: A limitations section: 47 spots from 13 brand YouTube channels (selection by what brands upload, not TV airtime); 1 fps sampling; the choice of k = 5; hue distance undefined for achromatic palettes (AAA Auto's greys); 24 of 30 homepages; UMAP on 54 points; the tool not validated against any outcome.
Uncertainty on any figure: bootstrap intervals by brand, or at least per-brand counts, since 5 Albert spots drive the >100° group.

Literature on advertising colour and brand recognition (e.g. Labrecque & Milne 2012 on colour in marketing; Gorn et al.), on music in advertising (Bruner 1990; Alpert & Alpert), and on distinctive brand assets (Romaniuk).
A clear statement of the kind of piece this is: a descriptive hub over four exploratory studies, not a test.

silent-detector.html.one_line: A useful negative result with a clean design (GroupKFold by question, abstention-pack leakage caught). It is undermined by a private repository, no intervals, best-of-8 selection reported as 'the' AUC, an uninterpreted anti-learning artefact, and a dismissive reading of its own most interesting number.
must_fix: Reproducibility. r1 says 'quaesitor (private) repository', so detector.py, the tests and the 125 run reports cannot be checked by a stranger. Make the parsed feature table and detector.py public, or state plainly that only detector.json is released and the analysis is not reproducible.
No uncertainty. With 87 questions and 5 folds, report the fold-to-fold SD or a question-level bootstrap CI for every AUC. The differences 0.55 vs 0.56 vs 0.64 may be within noise.
Selection. 'The best held-out AUC is 0.64' is the maximum over 4 feature sets × 2 model families, so it is optimistically biased. Say this, or use nested selection.

Within-pack AUCs of 0.29 (e-commerce) and 0.12 (taxi) are far below 0.5. They are presented as 'a query shape that means wrong for one question means right for the next'. An AUC of 0.12 under leave-group-out CV with few groups is a known anti-learning artefact: class balance shifts between folds. Report the number of questions per pack and treat it as an artefact, not a finding.

The reading of the filter result is misleading. detector.json shows the best model at threshold 0.5 forwards 3.4 % of answers at 86 % precision and 16 % recall of correct answers, against an 18 % base rate, a lift of about 4.7×. 'it keeps almost nothing' hides this. Report precision and recall, and say what a 3 % high-confidence lane would be worth.

Tautology or overclaim in the conclusions: 'a silently wrong number is by definition one that leaves no trace in how it was produced'. The data show AUC 0.64 > 0.5, so some trace exists. Rephrase as weak signal.

The repeat-sampling setup is not reported: temperature and seed of the three repeats, and the model names behind 'model alias'. Self-consistency depends entirely on sampling temperature. At temperature 0 agreement is trivial and the negative result is uninformative.

Not pre-registered and done in 'a day's work': state that the analysis is exploratory, list the 0.81 → 0.58 abstention correction as a post-hoc change, and mention the two excluded packs (<100 numeric answers) in the body, not only in r2.

Slogans and closing morals: deck 'for reasons that are more useful than a yes would have been'; 'consensus among three copies of the same blind spot is not evidence'; 'makes reconciliation a measured obligation rather than a hope'; 'The detector was worth building because it shows, with numbers, why the expensive check is necessary'; 'and that made the question worth a day's work'.
cut: Short-version box: it repeats the deck and facts almost verbatim (5 794 / 3 839 / 0.64 / 21 % vs 18 %). Cut it.
The meta-description repeats the deck with slogans. Shorten it.
The '.stack' line ('4 new tests, 732 in the repository') is portfolio decoration. Keep the test path in the references.
The self-promotional tie-in to 'the headline of the Quaesitor texts, that trust grows faster than accuracy'. That claim is not tested here; cite it only.
missing: Literature. Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022); LLM calibration and knowing what they know (Kadavath et al. 2022); semantic entropy (Farquhar et al. 2024, Nature); selective prediction and abstention; text-to-SQL error analysis (BIRD, Spider 2.0). The contribution relative to these, a negative result for SQL answers on planted traps, is not stated.

A per-trap breakdown (SCD, soft delete, currency, timezone, denominator) of agreement-conditional accuracy, since the mechanism claim ('ignoring the SCD duplicates on every attempt') is asserted without a number.

A 'What this does not show' section in house structure, with the limitations split out from the 'Consequences' section. The binary label, planted traps vs production, hand-written features and a single harness are already listed; add the unknown sampling temperature and the model set.
Calibration or reliability of the best model: detector.json has Brier scores and AP that are unreported (AP_correct 0.34 against a 0.18 base rate).
An access or run date range for the 125 runs.

ai-over-data.html.one_line: A practitioner case study titled 'measured' that reports no measurements of the system it describes. The only outcome numbers belong to Quaesitor, and sections 2 to 5 largely repeat engineering.html section 7. Either publish anonymised eval results or reframe it as a short design note.
must_fix: Title and deck promise 'measured' and 'measured it before anyone trusted it', but the text gives no result for the work assistant: no golden-set size, no correctness, silent-failure or refusal shares, and no before/after for the rebuild. 'Reached parity on the golden sets' (sections 2 and short box) has no n, metric or tolerance. Report at least relative or anonymised figures, e.g. 'n golden questions; correct x %, silent y %, refused z %, before vs after', or retitle.

Section 1 says 'These three numbers are how the product is measured, and every decision below was made to move them', yet none of the three numbers ever appears. Readers take this as a promise the page breaks.

Section 4 opener 'Each change in this section followed a measurement rather than a checklist' overclaims. The 40-to-15 tool cut and the confused-deputy fix are design reviews, not measurements; only the $21 / 4.07 M token cap came from a measured incident. Rephrase so it holds for each item.

Section 3 misquotes the source: 'silent-failure rate of frontier models ranges from 56 % to 92 % depending on the pack'. silent-detector.html says 'depending on the model and the pack'. Fix the attribution.
The deck's unsupported claims 'The most common AI system in a company today' and 'It is also the easiest one to ship wrong' either need a citation (a survey) or should be cut.
The stack line says quaesitor-method has '700+ tests', but engineering.html section 11 and reference 3 say the harness has '524 tests'. Pick one figure, dated.

Section 6 uses a hypothetical number as if it were evidence: 'a model that is confidently wrong 60 % of the time can have a demo that looks perfect'. Either tie it to the measured Quaesitor range or drop the figure.
'sitewitness ... with the five rules enforced in code': the five rules are never listed. Section 6 gives about six imperatives and the Ask paragraph four properties. Enumerate them or drop the count.

House-style violations: slogan paragraph openers ('A number from an LLM is a claim, and the protocol turns it...'), a rhetorical 'not X but Y' ('rests on the protocol around the model rather than on the model'), a closing zinger ('so build the cross-check instead of hoping'), and a triad in the deck ('built one, measured it..., hardened it..., and what I would tell...').

The short-version box repeats the deck and the facts strip almost line for line: 4 500 → 400, 40 → 15, $21 / 4.07 M, 14 fields, 56–92 %. On a 1 800-word page that is a third copy. Cut the box or make the deck the only summary.
cut: The 'Overwhelmed? Here's the short version' box (it is triplicate with the deck and the facts strip).

Section 6 in its imperative-list form ('Measure before you trust... Put knowledge... Treat the agent... Cap everything...'): it is a bullet list disguised as prose and restates sections 3 to 5. Keep at most two sentences that add something new.
The sitewitness/Ask paragraph: move it to a one-line cross-link. It advertises a different project.
The facts-strip item 'public counterpart 5 794 answers': it belongs to silent-detector, not to this system.

Duplicate passages shared verbatim with engineering.html (the confused-deputy sentence, 'silently and non-deterministically discarded results', and the POC/glossary paragraph). Keep them here and cut them there, or the other way round.
missing: Outcome table for the work system: golden-set size, how the questions were sampled, and the correctness / silent-failure / refusal / protocol-compliance shares, before vs after rebuild and hardening (anonymised or relative if necessary).
Definition of 'parity': same answer on what share of questions, and within what tolerance.
The reconciliation rule: what counts as agreement with a certified dashboard (exact, a relative tolerance?) and how often a certified figure exists at all (coverage).
Cost per run distribution after the caps (median and p95), since cost is described as 'a first-class field of every trace'.

Positioning against existing practice and literature: text-to-SQL benchmarks (Spider, BIRD), semantic-layer approaches (dbt Semantic Layer, LookML), and the Vanna/RAG pattern it replaced, with a sentence on what is new here.
Dates: when the rebuild shipped, when the $21 incident happened, and when the caps went in.
A limitations section as its own heading. The only caveat now sits in the short box and reference 1.

engineering.html.one_line: A CV page that calls itself an advertisement. It works as a hub but has no research question, three of its eleven sections duplicate ai-over-data and cutover, and it is full of the slogans the house style bans. Cut it to a lean overview that links out.
must_fix: The deck says outright 'The page is long on purpose, because it is the one page on the site that is allowed to be an advertisement.' That sentence undercuts every other page's claim to measured tone. Delete it and let length follow content.
The title 'The platform is code. So is the trust.' is a slogan pair, which the house style forbids for headings. Use a content title, e.g. 'Data and cloud engineering at Alma Career, 2025 onwards'.

'Byte-identical' (short box and section 6) and the meta description's 'proven to the byte' overclaim. The evidence is 'zero mismatches across twenty columns' plus day fingerprints, and cutover.html itself uses float tolerances. Say 'zero mismatches across 20 columns'.
The facts-strip label 'clouds, one platform / AWS + GCP' has lost its number. '0 / 0 mismatches' is unreadable notation: write '0 mismatches'.
Test counts conflict: section 11 and reference 3 say the Quaesitor harness has '524 tests', ai-over-data.html's stack line says '700+ tests'. Reconcile and date it.
Voice is inconsistent. The short box is in third person ('the author's own records... presented as her account') while the body and references are first person. Pick one.

Number style is inconsistent with the companion pages: 'forty tools, eighteen of which' and 'fifteen-tool' here, '40 MCP tools, 18' and '15-tool' in ai-over-data; 'fourteen fields' vs '14'. Choose one convention site-wide.

House-style violations: 'A prompt is a suggestion. IAM is a wall.' (closing zinger, short declaratives), 'since no customer has ever complained about CPU', 'as it used to on a normal Tuesday', 'the answer is always "the workflow, at 03:00, here is the log"', 'Nothing on the platform exists only in a console; the repository is the inventory.', 'The cutover I am proudest of was uneventful by design.', 'where it is newer and rarer' (unsupported), and 'Onboarding is an access-design problem as much as a documentation problem'.

The claim 'uv took lockfile resolution from about thirty seconds to under one per app' has no measurement method (cold or warm cache, how many apps). It also cites reference 2 (Zensical/Diátaxis), which does not support it.
Section 6 has no link to cutover.html, the public tool built from exactly this method (0 links found). Section 7 links ai-over-data but then repeats it anyway.
cut: Section 7, apart from the one-line pointer. It restates ai-over-data sections 2 to 5 nearly verbatim (4 500 → 400, the trust layer, $21 / 4.07 M, the third-party MCP schema defect, the POC and glossary).
The second paragraph of section 4 (the AI-agent access paragraph), which duplicates ai-over-data section 4. Keep a single clause and a link.
The second paragraph of section 6. Replace it with a link to cutover.html, which does this properly and reproducibly.
Section 9 'How I work': a creed list in prose form that repeats sections 1 to 6 ('infrastructure as code, always', 'no cutover without parity').
Section 11 'What runs this site': move it to the status or about page. It is about the site, not the day job, and repeats the watch, surf and hockey material from their own pages.
Most of the section 10 detail, down to one short paragraph of dated roles. Conference talks and C++ 'zero-defect' belong in a CV.
The stack line 'earlier:' list.
The short-version box, which repeats the facts strip (AWS+GCP/WIF, 40→15, 0 mismatches / 62 of 62, 4 500→400, $21).
The facts-strip items that duplicate other pages ('NL→SQL service, rebuilt', 'one unbounded question $21').
missing: Links from section 6 to cutover.html and from section 7 to ai-over-data only (a one-line pointer instead of a summary).
Dates for the key events (the dbt cutover, the GA4 backfill, the Dependabot cleanup) so that '792 → 332 and falling' has an as-of date.
A short, explicit 'what this does not show' paragraph near the top rather than only in reference 1: the figures are unverifiable self-report and the systems are not public.
A decision on the page's category. It is a hub or CV page and should be labelled as such, kept outside the research and journal set, rather than presented as an article.

cutover.html.one_line: The strongest of the three: a small, reproducible tool with a clear method, public code, a demo script and published reports. It needs positioning against existing data-diff tools, a justified tolerance, a benchmarked scale claim, a fixed reference and a shorter header.
must_fix: Reference 1 cites engineering.html 'sections 6 and 11' for the two work cutovers, but section 11 is 'What runs this site'. Cite section 6 only.

The half-cent fare tolerance is under-justified. The article says every mismatch is float noise with a maximum difference of 3.6 × 10⁻¹², yet it declares 0.005, which is nine orders of magnitude looser and would also hide real cent-level differences. State the actual reason, which the demo script's comment gives (the new side rounds to cents and the legacy does not). Alternatively show that a tolerance of 1e-9 also passes.

The '12.06 arriving as 12.059999999999999' example sits right after 'the largest absolute difference is 3.6 × 10⁻¹²'. That example's difference is about 2 × 10⁻¹⁵, so the pairing implies it is the maximum. Separate the two.
The tolerance formula has both τ_abs and τ_rel, but the CLI example '--tol amount=0.01' and the demo's '--tol fare=0.005' do not say which one they set. Document the CLI mapping.
'Fine for tens of millions of rows but not for billions' is asserted without a measurement. Give a timing and memory benchmark (rows, columns, machine, seconds, peak RAM) or soften the claim.
Run 1 is described as 'three findings, none of them planted', but the third, the row set, is a matching result plus a note about the source, not a finding. Say two findings and one observation.
The short-version box is a third copy of the deck and facts strip (six steps, 5 years / 20 columns, 62 of 62, 343 mismatches, 33 / 33, 41 tests, the limits). Cut it or cut the facts strip.

The TLC data reference has no access date and names no file (yellow_tripdata_2025-01.parquet). The package reference gives no version: the reports were produced with cutover 0.1.0 on 2026-09-14, so state that.
cut: The short-version box.
The anecdote 'which is what the first version of the tool did on the demo before the demo corrected it'. Either keep it as a dated entry in a changelog or cut it.

The closing sentence of the first section, 'In neither case did the argument for the cutover rest on having tested it; in both it rested on a count of differences, and the count was zero.' It is a rhetorical 'not X but Y' closer.
The phrase 'now with a certificate' in the limits paragraph (a zinger).
The stale unlinked files assets/cutover/report.html and report.json, which sit next to report-1 and report-2 (repository housekeeping).
missing: Related work: how cutover differs from datacompy, Datafold's open-source data-diff (hash bisection across databases), dbt-audit-helper (compare_relations), Great Expectations and SQLMesh table_diff. Without this the contribution is unstated.
A benchmark supporting the scale limit.
The exact hash used for fingerprints (algorithm, how rows are serialised, NULL and float encoding), so that '62 of 62 days' is reproducible outside the tool.
How NaN, ±0.0 and timezone-aware timestamps are treated in the column and fingerprint steps.
A one-line reproduction command for the demo (e.g. 'uv run tools/cutover_demo.py') with the expected runtime and download size.
A statement that the two work cutovers were not run with this package (the package postdates them), so the tool is validated only by its tests and the taxi demo.

prague-council.html.one_line: The strongest of the three: a clear question, honest design and good prose. Two things must be fixed before it is journal-ready: the headline overstates H1, and the pre-registration cannot be verified from the public repository.
must_fix: Pre-registration cannot be verified. 'How this was done' says the design was 'committed to the site's public repository before any vote was modelled', but git history shows docs/research/prague-council-design.md arriving in the same commit as the results and scripts (5a34401, 2026-09-28). Either link a registration commit or hash dated before the results, or reword to 'written and reviewed before modelling; not independently timestamped'. This applies to the 'pre-registered' kicker too.

Say in the article that the four-term fall in votes against (1.06 to 0.28 per 100) was already published and seen when H1 was registered. Design §0 records this; the article does not. H1's direction was therefore partly known in aggregate.

H1 is overclaimed in the deck and the short version: 'the same councillors vote against about half as often in each new term'. The article's own decomposition says otherwise. 2010–14→2014–18 was a fall to a fifth, 2014–18→2018–22 showed no change among stayers, and 2018–22→2022–26 fell to about two thirds. The result also fails among the 26 whose status did not change (× 0.86, p = 0.14) and weakens to × 0.72 without the first transition. Rephrase as a pooled average driven mainly by 2010–14 and flag the heterogeneity in the deck.

Causal slide in 'Yes votes in the coalition and in opposition'. The text says 'this comparison is not a causal estimate', then in the next sentence 'puts a list's voting ... down mostly to its seat in or out of the coalition rather than to its programme'. Cut the second sentence or make it descriptive.

The title 'Prague's council rarely says no' is true only of the files, which hold 55–67 % of roll calls: final votes on adopted resolutions, with procedural votes and amendments excluded, where 'government and opposition fight most'. Qualify the deck, for example 'on the resolutions it adopts', so the title does not overstate.
No references carry an access date, although open data (lkod.cz, golemio CSV, praha.eu councillor list 'as of September 2026') changes over time. Add 'accessed <date>' to refs 1, 10, 13, 14 and 16.
Explain the hypothesis numbering gap (H1, H3, H4) in the tests table: say that H2 was the demoted abstention hypothesis.
cut: The 'Overwhelmed? Here's the short version' box repeats the deck and the six facts almost word for word (88 %, 1.06→0.28, × 0.49, 95/59 %). Drop it or cut it to one or two sentences that add nothing already in the header.
'the dataset's contact at City Hall is the right person to ask' at the end of 'What this does not show' is off-register. Cut it.
The 'Corrected 29 September 2026' note sits in the middle of 'What changed after registration'. Move it to a dated correction line at the foot, as the house pattern does.
'Every councillor' table intro: the column definitions duplicate the table footnote. Keep one of them.

Trim the fig. 3 caption's speculation ('a change in the voting system or the rules of procedure would produce it, and this text has not found one'), which the 'Abstentions before and after 2018' section already covers.
missing: A reproduction note: environment and dependencies (the repo has no README or requirements file), the order in which to run the six scripts, and where the raw files land. figures.py, figures_extended.py and titles.py are used but not listed.
Links from the script names to the files on GitHub (they are plain text now).
Uncertainty on the descriptive headline rates (88 %, 0.28 per 100) and on the H3 error differences (10 and 6 fewer errors per 100), or a statement that they are population counts, not estimates.
A per-transition table or interval for H1 (fig. 4 shows it, but the text should give n and CI for each of the three transitions).
A one-line contribution statement against the literature: what a municipal assembly adds to Hix–Noury and Theriault.

prague-rings.html.one_line: The design and data work are solid, and the composition result (θ = 0.43) is a real contribution. The title and header claim more than the registered results allow, and the turnout and minor-party material should be cut back.
must_fix: The title 'Prague votes in rings, not along lines' asserts the metro null that H2 could not establish ('not supported: inconclusive', p = 0.28, 'a negligible metro effect cannot be told from a small one'). The strongest gradient in the article is housing type (the estates), not rings. It also uses the 'not X, but Y' device the house style bans. Retitle around the estates finding.

The facts line 'never half' ('31–44 % in 48 specifications; never half') and the short version's 'never half' are contradicted by the body. With age added, composition explains 52 %, 'and the test can no longer tell the answer from one half'. State that the registered block excludes age and that adding age reaches about half.

Pre-registration cannot be verified. The article says the design was 'committed ... before any census count or earlier election was joined', but docs/research/prague-rings-design.md first appears in the same commit as the results and scripts (1283162, 2026-09-28). Provide a dated registration commit or hash, or soften the claim.

H4 (turnout) is compromised by the article's own finding that the published register count includes voting-pass voters. It should be labelled uninformative rather than presented as 'not supported, sign reversed', or both tests should be described as unable to test the hypothesis.

The claim that '43 % is a lower bound on what composition explains' rests on classical measurement error in the controls. With 1 km cells allocated dasymetrically by flats, the allocation error is correlated with the housing measure, so the direction of the bias is not guaranteed. Either justify the claim or call it 'likely understated'.
Reference numbering is out of order: ref 22 (Part 1) is the first citation in the text. Renumber by first appearance.
No access dates on any data reference (ČSÚ open data, RÚIAN map service, PID GTFS, which changes daily and is why Flora is missing). Add them, and pin the GTFS snapshot date.
'Planners and campaigns both treat the metro as the city's spine' is uncited. Cite it or cut it.
cut: The short-version box repeats the deck and facts (26 %/16 %, 43 %, 0.55→0.80, −0.17). Remove it or reduce it to one sentence.

The minor-party paragraph (STAN, Stačilo!, SPD, Motorists; R² 13–29 %; the 'metro's one measurable trace' for SPD) is a forking-paths aside with no registered role. Cut it to one sentence or move it to a footnote.
The intro and first section describe the map twice: the fig. 1 caption and the paragraph that follows both explain the party picker and hover.
'Housing stock or residents' restates the registered questions already listed in the opening paragraph ('asks four things...'). Merge them.
'Turnout in the centre': compress it to a single paragraph with the caveat first, given the contamination.
In 'Robustness checks', the line on the placebo that was not run (line D) belongs in 'What changed after registration'.
missing: The effective sample for the headline tests: 282 clusters, but inference is over 57 districts. State that clearly in the facts, not only in the table note.

A reproduction path: repo README and dependencies, order of rings_data → rings_power → rings_extended → rings_robust, raw-file hashes, and links to the scripts. metro.py and figures_rings_extended.py are not all linked.

For H3, a note that matched precincts are unrepresentative (40 % vs 27 % panel) and that the 2021 census is fixed, so steepening could be compositional change. The text half-says this; the header should not present 'steepened' without that caveat.
A contribution sentence: what Prague adds relative to Maxwell (2019) and the context-vs-composition literature, beyond a local replication.
Units in the facts: 'points per 10 pp' and 'pp per pp' are both used. Harmonise them.

prague-districts.html.one_line: Two pieces are glued together: a useful descriptive note on district budgets, and a registered alignment test that by design could only detect effects two to three times the published ones, whose estimate then went through three post-result corrections. Report it honestly and much shorter as a registered null, with the budget description as a brief lead.
must_fix: The interval '−115 to +21 %' goes below −100 %, which is impossible for grants in levels. Explain that effects are linear differences scaled by the controls' usual grants and can therefore exceed −100 %, or report them on a scale that respects the bound. As printed in the facts box it reads as an error.

Pre-registration cannot be verified. The design says 'registered, version 2 (29 September 2026)', and the only commit of docs/research/prague-districts-design.md (ff0f0ca) also contains the results and scripts. A fix commit (9b3ce92) with 'flow direction, resolution dating' corrections also exists. Give the timestamped registration hash, or drop 'pre-registered' from the kicker in favour of 'design written before analysis, then corrected after results (three disclosed corrections)'.

The headline estimate is fragile, and the header does not say so. Dropping one control district (Troja) moves it to about 0 %, dropping ODS districts turns it to +14 %, and the 2023 window was cut to one year (agreement 0.79 < 0.9), so power is below the simulated about 100 % MDE. Put the 'uninformative/underpowered' reading in the deck instead of 'detects no such premium', and do not lead the facts box with −37 %.

The literature benchmark is cherry-picked in the facts ('published premiums are a third to a half'). The body cites Portugal at 19 % and Germany at −20 to −40 % under one bloc. Give the range honestly.

Mayor coding by 'two independent coding passes by a language model' is not independent coding (same model family). Call it double-coded by an LLM with hand adjudication, and move it to 'What this does not show' as a limitation.
The 'Correction, 28 September 2026' paragraph sits after the references. Move it to 'What changed after registration' or a dated correction line above the footer.
No access dates on MONITOR, ČSÚ population tables or praha.eu closing accounts, all of which are revised. Add them.
cut: The parsing-error story (25 m → 4.1 bn, H1 +19 % → −38 % → −37 %) is told three times: in 'How this was done', in the tests-table note, and in 'What changed after registration'. Keep it once, in the changes section.
The short-version box duplicates the deck and facts almost line for line (8 346–17 604, 35 320, 76 %, −37 %, −115 to +21 %). Remove it.
'Budget plans, capital spending and the 2024 formula' is three unregistered descriptive asides (54 of 57, 47 % capital execution, the formula change). Cut it or move it to a notes piece.
'What the districts spend on', and the table intro, can shrink to two sentences, since the table carries it.
In 'Robustness', the paragraphs of alternative estimators (−13 %, −14 %, placebo −18 %, switch-out −7 %, MONITOR side −2 100 CZK) can become one compact table.

The kicker ('Part 3 of 5 · city-district budgets, 2022–2024 · pre-registered · the city's grants to its districts, 2015–2023') is overloaded; shorten it. Also shorten the deck, whose final sentence runs past 60 words.
missing: A clear statement early on that the study was underpowered at registration (MDE ≈ 100 % vs literature 19–47 %) and why it was run anyway: the registered-report rationale.
The title 'One city, 57 budgets' does not signal the alignment question, which takes up most of the text. Retitle, or split the budget description into a separate note.

A reproduction path: nine scripts in tools/praha/ listed as plain text with no order, no README or dependencies, and MONITOR scraped through its public interface (state the endpoint and the date of scraping, and publish the raw extracts or their hashes; docs/research/prague-districts-files.sha256 exists but is not linked from the article).
The series is labelled 'Part 3 of 5', while the footer links Part 6 and there is no Part 5. The same inconsistency appears in the other parts; fix the numbering series-wide.
Per-resident CZK equivalents for the headline percentage effect, so readers can judge the magnitude.

prague-housing.html.one_line: There is a real, registered study here with one defensible result (the permit-to-house-number lag), but the title and deck frame Prague as an under-builder when the article's own European evidence puts its metro region in the upper quarter. The only supported test rests on a lag model the text itself calls degenerate, and about a third of the page reports uninformative results at full length.
must_fix: Title and deck contradict the body. 'Prague builds two homes for Vienna's three' and the opening fact cards set Prague against two hand-picked comparators. In 'Prague among 208 European metropolitan regions' the text says Prague's region 'places it 163rd of 208 from the bottom, in Europe's upper quarter', and 'Prague built the second most of the 14 Czech regions per resident'. The deck must say that Vienna and Warsaw are both well above the European median (the article itself says 'two metropolitan regions well above the European median of 3.55') and that Prague is above it too. Otherwise retitle around the pipeline finding.

Reconcile the H2 interval with fig. 3. The text says Prague's lag is weakly identified: 'anything from about 14 to 38 months fits almost as well, and Prague's fitted lag distribution is degenerate, with all its weight on one lag of 16 months'. Yet the difference has a tight 90 % interval of 8.7 to 12.6 months. With a 5-month rest-of-Czechia lag, that bounds Prague at roughly 17.6 months, which the profile likelihood does not support. Either the bootstrap understates uncertainty for a boundary or degenerate estimate, or the text is misdescribing the figure. Explain it, or report a profile-likelihood interval next to the bootstrap one.

State plainly what H2 identifies. The article concedes that 'five months is too short to build a block of flats, so outside Prague the fit probably also tracks common reporting timing' and that the lag 'may reflect project size rather than procedure'. If the comparator lag is partly a reporting artefact, '+11 months longer to be completed' is not a construction-time difference. The fact card '+11 months ... supported' and the lead in the short version need that qualifier, not only the body.
The intervals do not match the test level. H2 is tested one-sided at the Holm threshold 0.0167, but a 90 % interval is reported. Say which interval corresponds to the decision, or report both.

Label H5 consistently. The fact card says 'indeterminate', the table says 'not supported: indeterminate', the short version says 'indeterminate ... so the metro hypothesis is not supported', and the hub page says 'ended indeterminate'. Use one registered label everywhere and put the simulation-error caveat (0.0002 margin against about 0.0016 MC error) in the fact card as well.
The heading 'The five hypotheses and their results' conflicts with 'Only three hypotheses ... were kept as confirmatory'. Rename it to e.g. 'Registered tests and estimates'.

Disclose who the referees were. The design, the 'consolidated' referee reports (dated 29 Sep 2026), the registration and the results all fall within 28–29 Sep 2026, and the referees are described only by field. A journal-ready text must say who reviewed it, how independently, and on what timeline. If the reviews were automated or self-conducted, say so, because 'reviewed by three referees' otherwise reads as external peer review.

Git-based 'registration' should be described as a self-timestamped commit in a public repo, not as pre-registration in the registry sense (kicker: 'pre-registered'). Add a tamper-evident anchor (OSF, Zenodo DOI or a signed tag) or soften the wording.
Series numbering: the kicker says 'Part 4 of 5', but the series runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 6. Fix the numbering or explain the gap.
Add access dates to every web source (ČSÚ, Statistik Austria, BDL, ČÚZK RÚIAN, Eurostat tables). Give Eurostat table codes with URLs.
Reference r24 is defined but never cited (only r1–r23 appear in the text). Remove it or cite it.
'Warsaw, which built the most of the three cities, still had fast price growth' carries no number or citation. Support it or cut it.

football.html.one_line: There is a real finding here: the Czech Big-5 count fell in 2014/15 and, unlike its peers', has not recovered. But the article reports two break models and two gap decompositions whose numbers disagree, never names the 'nine strongest leagues', and draws a policy lever from reform evidence it admits does not hold.
must_fix: Two break models, two answers. 'Czech players in the Big-5 since 1995/96' reports a local-level model with two steps: the fall in 2014/15, x0.60, posterior 0.56. 'League strength estimated from players who moved' reports a one-step model: 2014-15, 62 %, x0.57 (0.38-0.86). Keep one model, or say explicitly that these are two specifications and why they differ.

Big-5 and top-9 are conflated. Para 3 of 'League strength...' says 'the count of Czech players in the top-9 leagues, 26 -> 6 -> 10 since 2007'. Everywhere else, 26 -> 6 -> 10 is the Big-5 series. Meanwhile 'Czechia has 26 such players' is the top-9 count for 2025/26. Readers will confuse the two 26s. Name the series consistently and relabel the 26 in each place.
The nine strongest leagues are never listed. Define them, with the UEFA ranking year, where the measure is introduced.

Internal arithmetic. 'Of the 192 mapped players, 27 play abroad, 63 % of them in a top-9 league' gives about 17 players. That contradicts '26 such players' in the top-9. Reconcile the pool definitions (country-page discovery vs the nationality column, r2) or correct one of the numbers.

The gap decomposition is inconsistent. 'Youth minutes, league strength...' says that against Norway 'home-league strength carries 73 % of a 7.0-per-million gap'. The later paragraph says Norway's +7.0 is 'mostly to U21 minutes (+4.2) and league strength (+5.1)'. Those sum to 9.3, which implies an unreported third channel of -2.3, and 'mostly to U21 minutes' contradicts the 73 %. Report all three channels with signs once, in one place. State that a ridge fit with three channels on n = 8 peers is descriptive.

The youth-minutes regression overclaims. The Bayesian HDI (-1.7 to +23.3, n = 8) crosses zero, while the 'pooled-panel OLS' interval (1.1-14.0) does not. Say how the panel errors were clustered by country; otherwise the OLS interval treats country-seasons as independent and is too narrow.

Causal drift. The article admits 'In neither country did the turn hold' and 'it is not a counterfactual'. It then says the sequence 'suggests that minutes for young players at home are the lever a federation holds'. The 'within reach' paragraph ('two regular under-21 starters per club ... a first move at 22-23') is policy advice, which contradicts 'gives no selection advice'. Cut both or downgrade them to a clearly labelled conjecture.

Reference r6 (FBref Big-5 tables) is never cited in the text; the Big-5 series cites r1 and r10 instead. r6 also says '2000/01 -> 2025/26', while the text says since 1995/96. Fig. 1 caption admits the image is the older 2000/01 render. Re-render the figure from the current series, or align the text to what the figure shows.
Access dates are missing. Only r1 has a read date. FBref (r2), Eurostat (r3), Wikipedia squad tables (r5, which need revision ids or a date) and UEFA coefficients (r7) all need one.

The kicker's '317 tests' reads as 317 statistical tests to a journal reader. They are software unit tests. Move the figure to the reproducibility paragraph and label it as such.

The duplicate statement of the gap decomposition. Keep one.

The CIES Football Observatory publishes expatriate counts and club-trained/youth-minutes indices per country; there is also work on league-strength equivalences (ClubElo, Opta Power Rankings) and plus-minus/mover identification. Cite them and say what is new.

A statement that the analysis is exploratory and not pre-registered, with the number of countries, editions and specifications tried (forking paths across 17 countries).

hockey.html.one_line: It is a competent descriptive tool write-up, not research. The headline counts contradict the article's own cohort tables, the novelty claim is unsupported, and the sensitivity claim overreaches; about a third of the text (graph, FAISS, LLM briefs) belongs in a project note.
must_fix: The defence counts contradict the tables. The facts strip, the short version and the text say 'four Czech defencemen in the NHL in total against Finland's fourteen'. The defencemen table sums to Czechia 0+1+1+1 = 3 and Finland 0+1+5+3 = 9; only Sweden's 30 matches. The Czech total also checks out only with 3: 12 forwards + 3 D = 15 = the stated 15 players. Fix the facts strip, the short version and para 3 of 'NHL players by position and age', or fix the tables.
Check the ages. The 26-29 cell names 'Pastrňák, Nečas, Zacha and Hertl'. Hertl (b. 1993) is 30+ in 2025/26, and Pastrňák turned 30 in May 2026. State the age reference date and re-bin.

The novelty overclaim. The deck says 'one number that nobody had aggregated'. NHL players per country by birthplace are routinely compiled (Hockey-Reference, QuantHockey, NHL.com). Drop the claim or state precisely what was not aggregated before (per-capita by position x age against named peers).

The sensitivity table does not support 'the map is not sensitive to the input I was least sure of'. The mean rank shift in the top 20 reaches 4.35 places. Only Liiga and Extraliga rows are shown, not NHL/AHL/SHL/NL/first league. The 'all -20 % / all +20 %' row is trivially zero, because uniform scaling cannot change ranks. Show all perturbed leagues, drop the trivial row and soften the claim.
The shrinkage is called 'empirical-Bayes', but K = 10 is fixed, not estimated from the data. Either estimate K (method-of-moments or a beta-binomial fit) or call it a fixed-strength prior.
Median P/GP in cells of n = 1 or 2 ('1 · 0.42', '1 · 0.00') is not a comparable statistic. Grey out or suppress medians below n = 3, or say that they are single players.
The per-capita count uses birth_country = CZE, while the mapped pool uses 'Czech eligibility'. State the difference and how many players it moves (e.g. Czech-eligible players born abroad).
Population denominators (r3) have no source. Name the source (Eurostat / national statistics / UN WPP) and the date.

Access dates for the NHL API, MoneyPuck, Liiga and hokej.cz are missing. Say whether the 18 May snapshot is committed so that 'make install && make all' reproduces the published numbers rather than re-fetching (r6 is ambiguous).

(throat-clearing); the section closing '...and the reader does not have to accept a single reading of the pool' (moral).

'The knowledge graph, similarity search and scouting briefs' (Neo4j, FAISS, LLM briefs, the 570-phantom-node bug) is engineering, not findings. Reduce it to one sentence with a link, or move it to a notes post.

The kicker's 'rendered 18 May 2026 · English edition 12 September 2026' duplicates r1.
missing: A stated research question and the contribution relative to existing work. Cite NHL-equivalency literature properly (Desjardins' league equivalencies, Sznajder/NHLe papers, hockeyviz as an actual page), not a homepage.
Year-to-year variability of the per-million counts. One season of 15 players is noisy, so show at least the 2024/25 value as well, since the data are already there.
Silhouette scores and the chosen k for the clusters, and a note that age is one of the four PCA features, which mixes profile and career stage.
A separate, specific limitations section. The current one mixes the two dropped analyses (good, keep them) with generic 'public data only' caveats.

weather.html.one_line: A careful verification protocol with no results yet (9 issue dates, already a five-day gap). The design has two leakage bugs, in lead-0 precipitation and in the persistence baseline, that would bias the very predictions it registers. Fix those and publish it as a dated note, then promote it once the gates open.
must_fix: Persistence baseline leakage. verify.py (the lines computing mae_tmax_persistence and brier_persistence) uses the observation of target - 1 day. At leads >= 2 that observation is not available at issue time, so persistence is given future information and becomes artificially strong at long leads. That directly contaminates prediction 2 ('persistence ... an easier one from lead 3'). Use the last observation available at issue (issue - 1 day).

Lead-0 precipitation is a hindcast, not a forecast. SRA for day D covers (D-1 06:00, D 06:00], but the collector runs at 06:40 UTC on D with past_days=1. Lead-0 rainfall is therefore entirely past hours, and lead-0 TMI/TMA windows are partly past. Drop lead 0 for precipitation (and flag it for temperature), or define leads from the window end.

The Brier probability double-counts ICON. The article admits 'best_match resolves to ICON for Prague', yet the formula uses f_i = #models / 4 with best_match included. ICON gets double weight, and the probability ladder is not what it claims. Use the three distinct models (f / 3) for the ensemble probability and keep best_match only as a separate column.

Predictions dated 15 September are not tamper-evident on the page. Link the commit (hash and timestamp) where they were written. Otherwise 'written before the first pair existed' is an assertion, not evidence.

The predictions are not decidable as written: 'clearly positive', 'about zero', 'at least as good'. Give the numeric criterion and the interval rule for each. Say what happens if the CI straddles the threshold (inconclusive).

Code facts are stale. 'The whole thing is 350 lines and five tests' and r2 '5 tests' vs the repo, which has 368 lines in collect.py + verify.py and six test functions in weather/tests/test_verify.py. The facts strip also says '5 tests'.

The data gap is not disclosed. data.json lists issues 2026-09-15 and then 2026-09-21 onward; 16-20 September are missing. The page claims a missed morning 'shows as a visible gap'. Say so in the text and state how many pairs this costs toward the 14/30 gates.
A block bootstrap by ISO week with 2-5 weeks of data is degenerate. Set a minimum number of weeks (e.g. >= 8) before showing an interval, not just a minimum number of pairs.

Overclaims and house style: 'in a way nobody can argue with' (a station point vs a model grid cell has a representativeness error, which the article's own Klementinum heat-island remark concedes); 'in return "skill" on this page means skill against the world' (slogan close); 'Running it costs nothing.'; 'it exists because the surf verifier was built as a general verifier rather than as a surf page' (closing moral); the title 'Weather, checked.' (slogan).
cut: The short-version box restates the deck, the window definition and the gates, which each have their own section. Remove it.
The comparison with the surf page appears three times (deck, short version, first section). Keep it once.
'The daily job' can shrink to two sentences (cron, append-only storage, gap policy) and move to the footer.
missing: Stating up front that this is a protocol with no results yet, and the date results are expected.
Citations for the station histories (Ruzyně since 1938, Klementinum since 1775) and for the Klementinum urban heat-island bias the first prediction relies on.
Representativeness: grid-cell elevation vs station elevation (364 m and 191 m), and whether any lapse-rate correction is applied.
Access dates for ČHMÚ open data and Open-Meteo, and the Open-Meteo model versions / resolutions at run time.
The verification literature beyond Wilks, e.g. Jolliffe & Stephenson (2012), and published ECMWF/DWD verification scores, to anchor the 1.0-1.6 °C prediction.
A power statement: what effect sizes (the ECMWF vs ICON MAE difference) are detectable with 30 or 90 pairs.
