site.standard:
EDITORIAL STANDARD, bsandova.com (v1, 29 Sep 2026). It applies to every page in All work. It supersedes the line 'Length follows from content. Nothing substantive from either version is dropped' in docs/style/long-articles.md. All other prose rules in that file stay in force site-wide, not only for Prague, measured.

1. KINDS. Every page is exactly one kind, which it shows in its kicker.
- RESEARCH: states a question and a design, and reports inference.
- TOOL: a public artefact with code, tests and a worked example.
- NOTE: a dated, descriptive or creative piece that makes no inferential claim.
- HUB: an index of other pages.
A page that cannot meet the standard for its kind is moved down a kind or retired, never published half-way.

2. LENGTH CAPS (body text, excluding tables, captions and references).
- Research: 2 500–3 500 words (thesis summary 1 700).
- Tool: 1 000–1 500.
- Note: 400–900.
- Hub: at most 1 000.
Exceeding a cap requires a stated reason in the change log.

3. HEADER, identical order on every page.
- Kicker: kind · series and part (if any) · object and period, at most 12 words, no status words such as 'pre-registered' unless §6 is met.
- H1: a content title that names the object and, for research, the finding or question. Not a slogan, not two sentences, no 'not X but Y', no trailing period.
- Deck: at most 2 sentences and 60 words, giving the question and the main result with its uncertainty and its registered label.
- Facts strip: at most 4 cards. Each card has a number, its unit, and its interval or the words 'administrative count, no sampling error'.
- The 'Overwhelmed? Here's the short version' / tldr box is abolished site-wide. The deck is the only summary.

4. METADATA BLOCK, placed directly under the facts strip, in mono, one line each.
- Published <date> · Updated <date> · Version <n> (link to the change log at the foot).
- Kind and status: for research, one of published / preprint / registered study / exploratory; for tools and notes, protocol / tool vX.Y / note.
- Registration: see §6. For unregistered work, 'Not pre-registered; exploratory'.
- Review: who reviewed it and how. For example 'Design reviewed by three LLM-simulated referee roles (subject, statistics, data) run by the author; no external peer review', or named reviewers with their affiliation. The word 'referee' is never used without this line.
- Data availability: sources with access or snapshot dates, the licence, and the hash list file (docs/research/*-files.sha256, linked).
- Code availability: repository path (linked), commit hash of the published version, and the one command that reproduces the page's JSON.
- How to cite: Šandová, B. (YYYY). Title. bsandova.com/texts/slug, version n, accessed <date>. A BibTeX link is optional.
- Licence: code under MIT, text and JSON under CC BY 4.0, stated once on every page.

5. BODY STRUCTURE.
Research sections, in order:
1. The question and contribution: 1 paragraph, positioned against at least 3 external references, never self-citations only.
2. Data.
3. How this was done: design, model, estimand, what t indexes, fixed effects, inference unit and effective n.
4. Registered tests and estimates, with the H table.
5. Results per question.
6. Robustness: as a table, not prose lists of variants.
7. What changed after registration: dated list, each change told exactly once.
8. What this does not show: limitations, all in one place.
9. Reproduction.
10. References.
11. Change log and corrections: dated, at the foot, never mid-text.

Tools: What it does and prior art (at least 2 comparable tools named) · Method, precise enough to reimplement · Worked example with real output · Evaluation or tests, with the measured error rate where one exists · Limits · Install and reproduce · References · Change log.

Notes: at most 3 sections, a dated kicker, and no statistical claims beyond descriptive counts with their source.

6. REGISTRATION CLAIMS.
- 'Pre-registered' may be used only with a tamper-evident anchor dated before any outcome data were joined: an OSF registration, a Zenodo DOI, or a signed git tag pushed to the public remote, cited by its id.
- A branch commit in the author's own repository is described as 'design committed to a public branch at <hash> on <date> (self-timestamped)'.
- Where the design first appears in the same commit as the results, as in Parts 1–4, the only permitted wording is 'design written and reviewed before modelling; not independently timestamped'.
- Everything the author had already seen when registering (for example, earlier published aggregates) is disclosed in the article, not only in the design file.

7. NUMBERS AND UNITS.
- SI spacing for thousands (10 565); % with a thin space; percentage points written 'pp'.
- One unit per quantity across the whole site. The same dataset has one name and one count everywhere.
- Every estimate has an interval, labelled by type: '95 % CI', '90 % CI (one-sided test at α)', 'Monte Carlo range over assumed inputs', 'bootstrap by <cluster>'. The level must match the decision rule.
- Population counts are marked as such.
- Effective sample (clusters and groups) is stated next to the headline estimate.
- Registered labels (supported / not supported / inconclusive / indeterminate / uninformative / underpowered) are used verbatim and identically in the deck, facts, table, body, hub and CV.
- No cross-family tallies such as '4 of 16'.
- Seasons as 2014/15. Dates as 29 September 2026.
- Every number in the prose is generated from, or diff-checked against, the published JSON.

8. FIGURES.
- Numbered in order of appearance. Each caption states what is plotted, its unit, n, the uncertainty band, and the source with its date.
- No 'from the first estimate' or superseded figures in a current article; those belong in the archived version.
- At most 6 figures in research and 3 in tools and notes.
- Every figure has a data-view hook to its JSON and alt text.
- Colours named in a caption must match the rendered palette.

9. REFERENCES.
- Numbered by first citation. Every entry is cited, and every citation resolves.
- One work per entry.
- Author (year). Title. Publisher or outlet. URL. Accessed <date>. Data sources add table code and snapshot date. Software adds version.
- Primary sources over explainers or commercial pages. Self-citations are allowed but never the only support for a claim.
- Private material is marked '(private; not verifiable)', and the claims resting on it are flagged in the text.

10. PROSE.
The long-articles.md rules apply site-wide: no slogans, no zingers or closing morals, no 'not X but Y' device, no personified data, no first-person lessons, no promotional adjectives ('proudest', 'world class', 'nobody had'). Also: no policy advice drawn from non-causal evidence; causal language only for identified effects; 'descriptive' said explicitly otherwise.

11. SERIES.
Parts are numbered by publication order with no gaps. Unpublished parts appear on the hub as 'in preparation' with their design link. Every part links back to the hub and to its neighbours.

12. GATE.
A page enters All work only after an editor checklist pass covering §3–§10: header, metadata block, one summary, caps, labels, intervals, references with dates, reproduction command, change log. The pass is recorded as one line in the page's change log ('Checked against standard v1 on <date>'). Pages that fail stay unlisted.
